verdict: Halliburton's revenue was flat as international growth offset weaker North America fracking, and it sees mid-single-digit growth in 2027.

segments.name: Completion and Production
segments.note: Cementing, stimulation (fracking) and finishing wells so they can produce.

segments.name: Drilling and Evaluation
segments.note: Drilling wells and measuring what is underground.

opex.name: Impairments & other charges
opex.note: Write-downs and other one-off charges taken this quarter.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the head office and support functions.

opex.name: SAP S4 upgrade
opex.note: Migrating the company's core computer systems to SAP S4.

otherDetail: Interest and other costs outside the core business, net — $111 million taken out of profit on the way to $513 million of pre-tax income.
follow100Note: Kept as profit is total net income of $419 million; $417 million of it is attributable to Halliburton shareholders.

takeaways.title: International did the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: International revenue rose 3% from last quarter to $3.5 billion, led by an 8% jump in Middle East/Asia, while North America fell 5% to $2.2 billion.

takeaways.title: Adjusted margin improved
takeaways.text: Excluding $107 million of impairments and other charges, operating income was $731 million — a 12.8% margin, up from 12.0% last quarter.

takeaways.title: 2027 outlook: margins near 15%
takeaways.text: Management expects mid-single-digit revenue growth in 2027 with operating margins of about 15%, assuming a flat North America market.

oneTimers: Results include a $107 million pre-tax charge for impairments and other items; excluding it and tax adjustments, adjusted net income was $501 million, or $0.60 per share.
